From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>

Subject: Renewal health & variable burn: proposed SLA/term flex path

Hi Liam —

Thanks for the heads-up on the upcoming renewal. I pulled a short usage health summary for Q3 (attached) and a suggested path that balances your burst patterns with a modest commit uplift + an SLA flexibility addendum. High-level notes:

- Token burn has 3 distinct peaks tied to night-batch reranking jobs; those compress into ~40% of your daily spikes.
- Average per-conversation tokens stable at ~1,600, but the tail weekly median increased 18% MoM.
- Current commit covers ~72% of expected steady-state usage; burst credits are the main lever for excess.

Proposal (attached doc):
1) 12-month term with a 20% commit increase to cover steady-state growth.
2) Add the SLO Flex Path (see spreadsheet) — maintains base latency SLA but provides a burst corridor (up to 2.5x for short windows) with tiered overage pricing and pre-authorized burst credits.
3) One-time operational credit of $10k to offset migration of the reranking jobs to a batched pipeline (we can walk ops steps if helpful).

I attached: acme_q3_usage_summary.pdf, proposed_term_addendum_v2.docx, and an SLO KPI workbook. Can we sync 30 minutes this week to walk through the numbers? If a contract team review is easier, I can route a redline to Contracts@acme-corp.com after we agree on the structure.

Cheers,
Rishi
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0127

Attachments: acme_q3_usage_summary.pdf (report), proposed_term_addendum_v2.docx (term language), slo-flex-path-kpis.xlsx (SLO/price model)

Rishi —

Appreciate the summary and attachments. Quick questions after scanning: 

1) The burst corridor sounds promising — how often in practice have other customers hit the 2.5x threshold? We need to understand worst-case impact on our monthly invoice.
2) Can you confirm whether the operational credit is a one-off credit applied to the first invoice after renewal?
3) On the 20% commit increase: can you show a sensitivity table for 10/15/20% so we can share with finance (we may not want to jump straight to 20% without seeing projected ROI).

We can do a quick SDR + Finance review on Thursday at 11am ET if that works for you. I'll loop in our internal infra lead if we need to talk batching migration specifics.

Thanks,

Rishi / team —

I pulled incidence from three customers with similar batch+burst profiles (anonymized):
- Customer A: hit >2x bursts 3 days/month on average; 2.5x threshold was rare (~1 day/month) tied to marketing spikes.
- Customer B: regular weekly spikes due to nightly jobs; 2.5x exceeded <0.5% of monthly minutes.
- Customer C: heavy experimentation; many short bursts but overall bill variance contained with pre-authorized credits.

Attached spreadsheet (slo-flex-path-kpis.xlsx) now includes a sensitivity tab that shows monthly invoice delta at 10/15/20% commit uplifts and three burst scenarios (baseline, 1.5x avg bursts, 2.5x extreme). Summary: a 10% commit with the SLO Flex Path reduces expected overage variance more than the 20% pure commit (because burst corridor buys temporary headroom).

I support offering a $10k one-time credit to help cover Ops work — it's an effective short-term incentive to move their reranking to a batched flow (which reduces their long-run unit costs). Marissa, sign-off?

Monica
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@acme-corp.com>, Contracts <contracts@acme-corp.com>

Thanks everyone — agreed path. Quick recap for the record and next steps:

1) Term & commit: 12-month renewal, initial commit +10% (we'll include a sensitivity appendix showing 15/20% outcomes).
2) SLO Flex Path: approved as a contractual addendum — maintains latency SLA, includes a burst corridor up to 2.5x for short windows with tiered pricing beyond pre-authorized credits. Karthik approved the SLO language; Contracts team, please proceed to redline.
3) Credit: $10k one-time operational credit applied as a contra on the first invoice after renewal effective date.
4) Ops migration: Monica will co-own a runbook with Acme infra for batching best-practices; aim for 60-day migration cadence to realize unit-cost benefits.

Rishi — please send the updated proposed_term_addendum_v2.docx (final redline ready for Contracts) and I'll mark as approved from GTM. Liam — once Contracts confirms signatures, we'll schedule the kickoff with your infra lead.

Marissa Cole
VP, Sales Operations — Redwood Inference
